comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4463 @ c205190fd

**Why it will be hard.**

1. **The real hub is `public/common.js`, not the bridge.** It sets 51 `window.*` globals and 29 renderers load it first. A view can't import from it while it stays a classic script. Making it a module in one go pushes all 51 globals through the one allowed bridge, and changes their timing on 28 unconverted pages: module scripts run after every classic script, the same trap the area note records for `window.CostFormat`. So "one view at a time" really means one view plus a step into the hub. In practice the single bridge ends up carrying common.js, not cost-format. Watch for anyone reading "one bridge" as "one bridge per module".

2. **Specifiers have to be settled before any view converts.** `cost-format-global.js` imports `'/shared/cost-format.js'`. In Node that resolves from the filesystem root, so a test can't import a page module that uses it. The choice is an import map (an inline `<script type="importmap">`, which needs a CSP hash, and `page.js` already has `scriptBodyHash`), paired with `package.json` `"imports"` for Node, or relative specifiers with a URL layout that matches the repo. This one decision settles whether "tests get simpler" can hold.

3. **The test seam breaks; it doesn't carry over.** 64 suites load scripts through `tests/unit/helpers/client-world.js` (a classic `vm` sandbox), and there are 85 `world.run` calls that reach script-scope `let` bindings. Module scope removes those, so each one becomes an export or goes. The area note asks for a "module-capable client test loader". I'd question that. `package.json` is already `"type": "module"`, so Node can `import` `public/*.js` directly with a fake-DOM global, provided a module doesn't touch `document` at load. A `vm.SourceTextModule` loader (behind an experimental flag) is the elaborate road the ticket says not to take.

4. **Some Waiting entries have nothing to do with modules.** The `llms.txt` drift, the no-AI "Next step" spinner, and app.js's whole-page `DOMParser` are real but sit outside this work. Close them separately or name them as out of scope. Folding them in makes the slices bigger without making the area cleaner.

**Symptom vs. cause.** The no-build rule is the stated target, but the pain reads as common.js being a 3,309-line pool of globals and "client twins". Modules are the tool for that. They aren't a fix by themselves: converting files without splitting common.js by concern just moves the pool.

**What I'd do first: one design piece, before any view converts.**
- Pick the specifier scheme (import map + `"imports"` vs. relative) and prove it with one page-module test that is a plain `import`.
- Replace `cost-format-global.js` with one general bridge file whose global list is the explicit ramp, plus a ratchet check that the list can only shrink. That settles the bridge Waiting entry and stops a second shim being written.
- Then the first view: a small one that already wants exports. Eleven files carry `typeof module … module.exports` dual exports (`question-cards.js`, `home-placement.js`, `close-out.js` are small). Convert it, rewrite its tests as imports, and name what was retired.
- Save `observation.js` (5,019 lines, about 40% comments by LIN-4446's count) and `common.js` itself for last. Finding out why observation.js is that size is a separate question from making it a module.

The leaf twins `lib/task-page-href.js`, `lib/timeline-zoom.js` and `lib/providers/models.js` import nothing, so they're cheap retirements once the bridge is general. `ship-layout` and `prompt-formatters` import other modules, so they still can't be served as single files.

## Survey global: LIN-4463 @ c205190fd

**Where it lands.** `public/`: 44 classic scripts, 35,245 lines. A month ago it was 39 files and 31,909 lines; three months ago 35 and 20,274. `common.js` grew from 1,795 to 3,309 lines and `observation.js` from 1,309 to 5,019. So it's getting bigger fast, but the rules are getting better: one fake DOM and one `loadWorld` under a census check, a leaf-purity check, and an allow-list instead of a served directory. The area already shares in **three ways**: `window.X` globals (about 50 from `common.js`, loaded by 29 renderers); `module.exports` scaffolding in `question-cards.js`, `home-placement.js` and `close-out.js`; and `/shared/` plus its bridge. The bridge has a test twin, `tests/fixtures/browser-cost-format.js`.

**Done the obvious way**, by converting a leaf like `home-placement.js` or `question-cards.js`, the work adds a **fourth** way and a second bridge. Their consumers (`app.js:816`, `prompt-section.js:1030`) are classic scripts reading `window.*`, and modules run after every classic script. That is the symptom under this ticket: converting leaves first makes bridges. **Converting top down doesn't.** A page's entry script (`app.js`, `task-page.js`) made a module runs *after* `common.js`, so it can read any classic global safely and import whatever has been extracted. A leaf becomes a module only once all its consumers are modules. Then the one bridge can only shrink.

**What must learn about it:** 29 renderer `SCRIPTS` lists; `shared-modules.test.js`, which hard-codes the shim, `'window.CostFormat'` and four consumers; the fixture twin; the area lesson "Views and the `vm` test loaders stay classic", which will be false; and `areas.json`, which maps `^public/` but gives a served `lib/` leaf no front-end home, with nothing to notice. About 20 tests grep `public/` source as text and some assert classic shapes.

**Specifier, settled cheaply:** key `SHARED_MODULES` at `/lib/cost-format.js` instead of `/shared/…` and keep views flat in `public/`. `import … from '../lib/cost-format.js'` then resolves identically in the browser (clamped at root to `/lib/…`) and in Node, since `package.json` is `"type": "module"`. That needs no import map and no CSP hash, and tests use plain `import`. A check should keep `public/` flat.

**Better, at this task's cost:** convert one page entry, top down. Retire `cost-format-global.js`, its test twin, and the `module.exports` blocks of what that page imports. Rewrite the stale lesson. Add a shrink-only check over the single bridge's names. Extract `common.js` by concern only as a converted page needs it: escape and format first, then the timeline maths twinning `lib/timeline-zoom.js`. Of the 89 `world.run` accesses, those reaching script-scope `let`s become exports or go.

**Better still, not this task's:** `observation.js`'s size (find out why first), `app.js`'s whole-page `DOMParser`, the `llms.txt` drift and the no-AI Next-step spinner. Defer those four Waiting entries by name rather than folding them in. The `ship-layout` and `prompt-formatters` twins need their `lib` side made a leaf first.

### Plan Review Verdict

**Verdict:** Approve. The plan's premises check out against main, and it meets the ask; the notes below are corrections the builder can make without changing what the plan decides.

**How it meets what was asked.** The ask says: "the slice 1 bridge is gone, or the only one left and shrinking under a check". The plan takes the second branch. `cost-format-global.js` stays the only bridge, with a bridge-inventory check, and drops from four consumers to three in piece 1. "One view at a time … whatever size is natural": the plan converts two views and lists the next ones in order. That is the ask's own grain, not a narrowing. "Waiting entries are settled, or say why not": all ten have a disposition. The brief's open question about Survey global ("retire cost-format-global.js at this task's cost") does not need John. The bridge has four classic consumers across six renderers, so converting one page entry cannot retire it, and the Done-when explicitly allows the "only one left and shrinking" outcome. The survey is advice, not a ruling.

**What I checked, at `5dcf5bcda`.** No file the plan touches has changed since the ticket was filed: `git log --since` over `public/ lib/ tests/ docs/ CLAUDE.md` shows only the merge `b708a9815`, which touches none of them.
- `SHARED_MODULES` is a one-route-per-file allow-list (`lib/vendor-assets.js`). There is no SPA fallback after `express.static`, so an unlisted `/lib/x.js` is a real 404. There is no `<base>` tag. CSP is `script-src 'self'` plus hashes. `public/` has no subdirectory `.js` files, so the flat rule holds today and `../lib/x.js` resolves the same way in the browser and in Node.
- `{ module }` emits `<script type="module">` (`lib/components/page.js:207`). `cost-format-global.js` is the only ESM file in `public/`.
- `workspace-kpis.js` reads only `__WORKSPACE_KPI_DATA__`, `HarbourCharts`, `Chart` and `CostFormat`. `common.js` and `app.js` set none of them, so running after them is safe.
- `task-page.js` reads classic globals only behind `typeof`/truthiness guards and assigns no `window.*`. It is the last entry in `SCRIPTS`, and its only load-time effect is one `DOMContentLoaded` listener (`:925`). So it converts without adding to the bridge, and its listener order is unchanged.
- The four `window.CostFormat` readers and six renderers match. There are ten Waiting entries; Lessons is 2,122 bytes. `CLAUDE.md:43` and `common.js:14` are as described. Node is v25 and `package.json` is `"type": "module"`, so a native `import()` with a `?v=` cache-bust works. `node --test` isolates each file in its own process, so globals a helper installs cannot leak between suites.

**Blocking findings:** none.

**Notes for the builder** (most important first)

1. **Witness 4 does not exist as described: rewrite it, don't just rerun it.** `tests/e2e/workspace-kpis.spec.js:211-227` asserts `window.CostFormat.formatUsd(0.004)` on the KPI page, and never looks at the cost axis. Piece 1 removes the bridge from that page, so the test as written fails with a TypeError. Replace it with a check that actually proves the new mechanism. It should assert all of these:
   - `/lib/cost-format.js` loads with 200 and a JavaScript MIME type (`page.waitForResponse`);
   - there is no `pageerror` and no CSP refusal;
   - the cost chart's y-axis formats with the shared formatter, e.g. `Chart.getChart(document.getElementById('chart-cost')).options.scales.y.ticks.callback(0.004) === '<$0.01'`.

   This is the only real-browser proof of a page module importing `../lib/`. If Playwright can't run in the session, write it anyway and say CI carries it.

2. **The import helper needs more than "fake DOM on globalThis"; build it in piece 1.** `task-page.js` uses bare `setTimeout`/`clearTimeout`/`setInterval`/`document`, and `window.api`. The suites the plan migrates depend on `loadWorld`'s `timers` collector and its window stubs:
   - `task-page-question.test.js:223` (`makePage`);
   - `task-timeline-client.test.js:207`;
   - `task-page-client.test.js:358/422/554`.

   `task-page-client.test.js:423` also runs the real classic `close-out.js` in the same world. Piece 1 has the same need: witness 3 needs `window.HarbourCharts`, which the current test gets by running the real classic `chart-helpers.js`.

   So the helper should take loadWorld's own `{ window, timers, globals }` options and install them on `globalThis`, with `window === globalThis` as loadWorld does. It should give one supported way to run a named classic sibling in that same realm (`vm.runInThisContext`), restore everything it replaced, and then import the page fresh. Its own test should cover both "two fresh imports share no state" and "globals are restored".

   The `loadWorld` census (witness 8) can't see complexity moved into this helper. Keep the helper small enough that each migrated suite reads shorter than before, and say so in the piece's description.

3. **Witness 6's timing predicate is wrong for two of the three consumers.** `observation.js` and `prompt-section.js` never branch on `readyState`. Their registered witnesses (`observation-scan-due.test.js`, `lin-3833-run-control.test.js`) prove the timing rule by loading the script first and installing the global afterwards; they never set `document.readyState = 'loading'`. Only `cost-format-consumers.test.js` (flight-companion) does. Use a predicate all three meet: the witness file loads the consumer and only then calls `loadCostFormat` from `tests/fixtures/browser-cost-format.js`.

4. **Keep the renderer-coverage half of the current shim guard.** `shared-modules.test.js:179-194` asserts that every script list naming a consumer also lists the bridge as a module. The new inventory check replaces the hard-coded strings, not this assertion. Piece 1 legitimately removes the bridge from `render-workspace-kpis.js`; this is the assertion that would catch an accidental removal from `render.js` and the others.

5. **Bridge discovery: scan the whole module, not just its top level, and match bare reads.** A `window.X =` inside a function in a converted module is just as much a bridge. On readers: `window` is the global object, so a classic file can read bare `CostFormat` as well as `window.CostFormat`.

6. **Witness 7 conflicts with a Waiting entry in another note.** `docs/areas/other-features.md`'s first Waiting entry has `lib/cost-format.js` as its first cited path, so `area-notes.test.js` check 3 fails once the file moves to a front-end area. Moving it settles that entry ("still in the catch-all"), so delete it and name it in what piece 1 retires. Read the `area-map-placement.test.js` pins first, as the plan says.

7. **`/shared/` references reach further than the plan lists.** Besides the allow-list, the bridge and its test, there are:
   - the comment in `lib/cost-format.js:12`;
   - `tests/unit/cost-read-census.test.js:15` and `cost-format.test.js:3`;
   - `tests/fixtures/browser-cost-format.js:3`;
   - `docs/areas/other-features.md:17` and `docs/areas/platform-and-plumbing.md:18`;
   - `docs/architecture/source-map.md:151,347`.

   The last one is outside witness 10's grep scope, so widen that scope from `docs/areas/` to `docs/`. Also update the source-map lines for `workspace-kpis.js`/`task-page.js` if they call them classic.

8. **Pins that will move.** `render-workspace-kpis.test.js:154` pins `/workspace-kpis.js` before `/common.js` by index. If the entry moves, update the pin to say what is true: a module's position in the list does not matter. `shared-modules.test.js:238` (`/lib/cost-format.js` is 404) flips to the 200 case. In piece 2, `lin-3975-task-run-control.test.js:586` and `no-page-wide-label-listener.test.js:247` read `task-page.js` source or the renderer's `SCRIPTS` as text; rerun them after removing the IIFE.

### Breakdown

The approved plan is split into its two pieces. Plan review Approve: comment `73a74028-bbe9-4a4a-b502-8ed268a6bd08`, rev 1.

| Subtask | Piece | Blocked by | Session fit |
|---|---|---|---|
| **LIN-4471**: `/lib/` serving, bridge and import checks, workspace KPIs as a module | 1, the foundation and its smallest real consumer | none, lands first | One session. The plan pairs the foundation (re-keying `/shared/` to `/lib/`, the import helper, and the import-layout, bridge-inventory, served-leaf-owner and loader-census checks) with one real page module, so the specifier scheme is proven by a real page in the same change. Every item is small and fully specified. |
| **LIN-4472**: task page as a module, its suites as imports | 2, one real page top down | LIN-4471 | One session. It converts one page entry, the last script of one renderer, adds nothing to the bridge, and migrates that page's suites onto piece 1's helper. |

**Re-grounding.** Since the ticket was filed, the only commits on main are `b708a9815` (a merge) and `e8e92d50a` (LIN-4456). Neither touches a file or line the plan names. `e8e92d50a` edits `docs/architecture/source-map.md`, but not lines 151 or 347. The `/shared/` references and the four `window.CostFormat` readers still match the plan as amended by review note 7.

**Where the review's notes went.** I folded the review's eight builder notes into the subtask that each one affects:
- Into LIN-4471: the rewritten e2e witness, the helper's requirements, the corrected witness-timing predicate, keeping renderer coverage, whole-module and bare-read discovery, the other-features Waiting entry, the `docs/`-wide URL scope, and the KPI order pin.
- Into LIN-4472: the run-control and label-listener text pins.

**Cuts to `## As asked`: none.** The plan and the review agree on this: two views plus a bridge that stays the only one and shrinks under a check meets "one view at a time" and the first Done-when branch. The blind-read Done-when is judged after both pieces land. It is not a build subtask.

**What follows (not created here; one ticket each, by the same recipe):** `flight-companion.js`, then `observation.js`, then the `prompt-section.js` chain (`app.js`, `swipe.js`). After the last of these, the bridge and `tests/fixtures/browser-cost-format.js` are deleted.

**LIN-4471 (piece 1) engineering decisions, recorded against the approved plan** (PR #2431, branch `feat/lin-4471-lib-serving-workspace-kpis`)

No cut to `## As asked`. The points below are how the plan was carried out, each with its reason.

1. **Tick-callback proof (the survey's open question).** The browser assertion is delivered as written, with a priced-usage seed rather than a different proof. One priced task goes through the runner's own usage endpoint (as `task-timeline.spec.js` does), so the cost chart draws and `Chart.getChart(...).options.scales.y.ticks.callback(0.004) === '<$0.01'` is read in a real browser. Passes locally (Playwright), and it fails with `Received "0.004"` under a mutation.
2. **`lib/usage-snapshot-intake.js` owner.** Assigned to Runs & dispatch (it is the feedback intake's counter). The whole other-features Waiting entry is therefore settled, which resolves the scope conflict between the ask's size note and the global survey.
3. **`lib/cost-format.js` owner.** Front end: server-rendered pages, beside `task-page-href` and `timeline-zoom`. The ask allows either front-end area.
4. **Census scope.** The ratchet counts suites that call `loadWorld` or run a `public/` source through a vm, by name (102 today), so both load routes are covered, as review note 4 asks.
5. **Witness 6 predicate.** Each registered reader's witness must call `loadCostFormat` after the consumer loads. `readyState` is not required, as review note 3 asks.
6. **`server.js:1227` comment** corrected (`/shared/*` → `/lib/*`) although it sits outside the acceptance grep.
7. **Retired-URL witness.** The one test that proves `/shared/` is gone builds the path from parts, so the acceptance grep stays empty. Flagged for the reviewer.

Piece 2 (LIN-4472) is unblocked: the import helper, the specifier rule, and the corrected lesson are in place.

### Engineering call: extract the served duration / relative-time leaf first (`lin4472-served-leaf`)

**Settled by autopilot, not escalated.** Scoping asked whether LIN-4472 may extract one small served lib leaf for duration and relative-time wording, given its Session-fit line says "no serving change".

**Decision: yes, extract it first.** The ask on LIN-4463 says shared logic is "imported, not restated" and that "each converted view drops its copies"; the task page restates two copies, so leaving them would contradict the ask. The serving path (`/lib/`, the `SHARED_MODULES` allow-list and its checks) already exists from LIN-4471, so this adds one allow-listed leaf, not a new mechanism. No view is retired, no product, money or authority question is involved, and the size record stays "Cuts: none". The Session-fit phrase predates LIN-4471 landing and is superseded by this note.

**If wrong:** the leaf is one file plus one allow-list entry and is easy to inline back.

## Review — LIN-4463

Parent review after both subtasks closed. Reviewed `origin/main` at head `0cf05ce8f5234277e5aecde1800f50f652131e33` (LIN-4472 squash). The parent has no PR of its own. The pieces are PR #2431 (LIN-4471, merge `17faa83f4`) and PR #2436 (LIN-4472, `0cf05ce8f`). Pre-work base: `c205190fd`.

CI: green. GitHub Actions "Tests" passed on `0cf05ce8f` (main), and both pieces were green on their merged heads, per their close-outs. Locally on main: bridge-inventory, front-end-import-layout, classic-loader-census, shared-modules and import-world pass 108/108.

### Done-when, item by item
1. **"the slice 1 bridge is gone, or the only one left and shrinking under a check"**: **met.** `public/cost-format-global.js` is the only module that writes a global, with `BRIDGED = ['CostFormat']`. Its readers went from four to three (`flight-companion`, `observation`, `prompt-section`). `workspace-kpis.js` and `task-page.js` are native modules. I mutation-checked `tests/unit/bridge-inventory.test.js` on main, and reverted both changes:
   - I added an unregistered `window.CostFormat` read to `public/app.js`. Two tests went red: "inventory is clean" and "exactly three classic readers".
   - I removed the `prompt-section` registration. Four tests failed.

   The check catches both growth and an unregistered reader. Piece reviews already covered the witness-order and renderer-coverage mutations. `/shared/` is retired. Production returns 404 for it and serves `/lib/cost-format.js` (LIN-4471 close-out).
2. **"the area's Waiting entries are settled, or say why not"**: **mostly met.** Ten entries went in. The bridge entry and the module-capable-loader entry are settled and deleted. LIN-4472 added the duration-copies entry. That leaves nine in `docs/areas/front-end-browser.md`. Each module-related entry now says why it waits: not a leaf, or its page is not converted yet. Two gaps remain (fixes below).
3. **"the area reads better in a blind read after this work than before it, by more than an untouched area read at the same times"**: **not met. No such read exists.** The per-PR blind reads on #2431 and #2436 both say "better". But they are diff reads, not area reads, and they have no control. `docs/plans/survey/area-read-reports/` has no `front-end-browser` report at any commit. The LIN-4464 baseline (`ce6cb88aa`) read `llm-and-prompts` and `front-end-pages` for LIN-4448, not this area. The brief and the Breakdown comment both say this item is judged after both pieces land. That time is now, and nothing has run it.

   **The usual control is no longer untouched.** Between `c205190fd` and `0cf05ce8f`, 11 files that map to `front-end-pages` changed. They include this ticket's own `lib/cost-format.js`, `lib/render-task-page.js`, `lib/components/time.js`, `lib/render-run-steps.js` and `lib/render-proxy.js`, and the new `lib/time-words.js` maps there too. I mapped every changed file with first-match over `areas.json` at `0cf05ce8f`. Only `task-model` and `auth-accounts-and-workspaces` have no changed file in that window, so the control must be one of those.

### What-was-asked, the remaining sentences
- *Pages become ES modules … no build step, no framework*: met for two views. There is no import map, no bundler and no `vm.SourceTextModule`.
- *Shared logic is imported, not restated*: met for the converted views. `workspace-kpis.js` imports `formatUsd`. `task-page.js` dropped `formatElapsed` and `relativeWords` for `lib/time-words.js`.
- *A bridge … one at most, and visibly shrinking*: met (see Done-when 1).
- *Tests get simpler*: met. The census fell from 102 to 100. The KPI vm/readyState suite is gone. LIN-4472 reports that every migrated suite is shorter.
- *One view at a time, each piece naming what it retired*: met. Both pieces have `Retires:` lines, and each one checks out against its diff (verified in the piece reviews).
- *No view retired; side rail and refresh come after*: met. No view was retired, and LIN-4342 and LIN-4343 were not touched.

### Regression check
`git log c205190fd..0cf05ce8f` over the touched front-end files shows only LIN-4471 and LIN-4472 commits, both on top of LIN-4446 (`92676b1fe`). None of them is a revert. The piece reviews confirmed that LIN-4446's serving rules (allow-list, raw 404s) and LIN-4040's close-out.js order are intact.

### Isolated, or one of a class?
The class is shared logic restated in classic scripts. The remaining instances are already Waiting entries with an unlock condition: the `session.js`, `observation.js` and `live-console.js` duration copies; the `common.js` twins; and `ship`/`ship-biscuit`. These are **inside** the ticket's class, but the approved plan bounds this ticket to two views and puts each of these in a named follow-up (flight-companion, observation, the prompt-section chain). The Breakdown and plan review recorded that bound with "Cuts: none". They are not ledger items.

### Fixes for the next stage (note-only)
- `docs/areas/front-end-browser.md`, the `public/brief.js` entry still ends "One shared reader in `public/common.js`." The plan's table said to rewrite it: one reader becomes possible only once `scan.js`, `recap.js`, `observation.js` and `brief.js` are modules that can import it. Rewrite it to say so.
- In the same note, the entries for `public/app.js` (DOMParser), `public/llms.txt` and `public/prompt-section.js` (no-AI Next step) don't say why this ticket left them. Add one clause to each: "not a module matter; outside LIN-4463 (plan table)". That satisfies "or say why not" in the note itself, not only in the plan comment.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside (Done-when 3).** The blind-read comparison has not been run. It is settled before close, not by filing a ticket. To settle it:
  - Run the frozen kit (`docs/plans/survey/area-read.md` and its reader prompt, blobs verified) on `front-end-browser` at `c205190fd` (before) and at `0cf05ce8f` (after).
  - Run the same kit on an untouched control at the same two commits. Use `auth-accounts-and-workspaces` or `task-model`, not `front-end-pages`, which this work changed.
  - Keep N = 14 and the same sampling rule. Record any adoption differences as LIN-4464 did, in an `area-read-adoption-*.md`.
  - The condition that separates right from wrong: the front-end-browser after-minus-before mean must beat the control's after-minus-before. If it does not, the ticket is not done.
- **Inside (from LIN-4472's close-out, still open).** The task page in Safari and Firefox (clock ticks, no console or CSP error), and owner and guest `/t/<token>` pages repainting through polling, were **not run**. Settle this after the deploy: an operator with a signed-in session opens a task page in each browser with devtools open. Rollback: revert `0cf05ce8f`.
- **Inside (from LIN-4471's close-out, still open).** A priced workspace drawing its cost chart in production with no console error was **not run**. Settle this after the deploy: an operator opens `/workspace/<key>/kpis` on a priced workspace. Rollback: revert `17faa83f4`.

### Verdict
Request Changes

Done-when 3 is unmet, and the ask names it as a condition of done. No implementation is missing. The missing piece is the paired area read described above, plus the two note-only fixes. Next action: `implementation` on LIN-4463, to run and record the paired area read and the note fixes. Then review re-runs. I raised no ruling: picking the control is an engineering call, settled here as the two untouched areas named above.

## Implementation: review items answered (PR #2439)

Continues the parent review `Review — LIN-4463` (Request Changes). The parent had no PR, so this PR carries the two outstanding items: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2439 (branch `feat/lin-4463-browser-area-read`, commit `964904710`). CI: all checks green, including `CI success`.

**Review finding → fix**
- Done-when 3, paired area read: run at `c205190fd` (before) and `0cf05ce8f` (after), frozen kit, N = 14, eight fresh readers. front-end-browser code +0.25 (3.125 → 3.375); control auth-accounts-and-workspaces 0.00 (3.25 → 3.25). ## As asked

**Repository:** JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

**What this is for.** John: "the UI issues trace back to one of my very first rules: no build step… it's the biggest target of the Theseus method… We don't need to tidy it all, but it's a perfect example where we can leave it better than we found it." The first slice (LIN-4446) served a pure server file to the browser at `/shared/` and retired the browser's copy. Its blind read found the cost: a bridge turns the shared file back into a global, with a load-timing rule that four files explain and nothing checks, and a second shared file would need a second bridge. On the direction, John: "I feel there's a sensible engineering approach, that a skilled developer would take… Excellent, that sounds like a great solution." Today the browser area has 44 script files that share through globals, `public/common.js` is 3,309 lines and `public/observation.js` 5,019, over 100 unit test files load browser scripts as classic scripts, and the area's note holds 10 Waiting entries.

**What we want.**

* Pages become ES modules that import what they share, as browsers do natively. Still no build step and no framework.
* Shared logic is imported, not restated: each converted view drops its copies.
* A bridge back to a global is only a temporary ramp for pages not yet converted: one at most, and visibly shrinking.
* The tests get simpler as views convert, not more elaborate.
* Taken one view at a time, each piece finishing one move and naming what it retired. John on size: "Happy for it to be whatever size is natural."
* No view is retired unless John rules it. The side rail and the visual refresh (LIN-4342, LIN-4343) come after, on the cleaner code.

**Done when**

* the slice 1 bridge is gone, or the only one left and shrinking under a check;
* the area's Waiting entries are settled, or say why not;
* the area reads better in a blind read after this work than before it, by more than an untouched area read at the same times.

**Every change names what it retires. Questions:** settle engineering questions yourself; only John's calls (product, money, authority, what to retire) go to him as rulings.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Size of the move

**Size:** just the task
**Why:** Views become modules one at a time under one shrinking, checked bridge, with waiting entries settled or explained; no survey finding binds beyond the ask, and the shared hub shrinks only as converted views need it.
**Cuts:** none
**Decided by:** the standing policy

## Implementation Plan

*Read at* `c205190fd` */ main* `5dcf5bcda`*. The only commit since this ticket was filed is a merge (*`b708a9815`*) that changes none of the files named below (*`git log --since=2026-11-13T15:39:22Z --stat` *over* `public/`*,* `lib/vendor-assets.js`*,* `lib/components/page.js`*, the two renderers,* `docs/areas/` *and* `shared-modules.test.js` *shows no file). Facts below were read from source, not from the surveys; where they agree with John's two surveys that is said, and where they differ that is said too.*

### What this is for, and what done looks like

The browser code shares through globals, so a page cannot import what it shares, and the one bridge LIN-4446 added (`public/cost-format-global.js` → `window.CostFormat`) carries a timing rule that four files explain and no check covers. This ticket makes the next move: pages become native ES modules that import, the bridge becomes a ramp that only shrinks under a check, and the area's notes tell the truth.

Done, as the ticket's own Done-when reads it:

1. The slice-1 bridge is the only bridge, its names are listed in one place, and a check fails if a name is added, if a name has no classic consumer left (so it must be deleted), or if a new classic script starts reading a bridged name without the timing rule's witness.
2. Each of the ten Waiting entries is settled or says why not (table below).
3. A blind read of the area after this work finds it clearer than before. That is judged by the reader, not built; the plan's job is to leave the stale statements (the lesson that views stay classic, the bridge entry, the loader entry, the comment in `common.js` saying `public/` cannot import a lib leaf) corrected.

**Cuts to** `## As asked`**: none.** The ask says "one view at a time" and "whatever size is natural"; this ticket converts two views and names the rest in order. That is the ask's own grain, not a cut. If John reads it otherwise, the ruling is "should this ticket convert every view" and the answer would be follow-up tickets by the same recipe, not a different plan.

### Answers to the brief's open questions (engineering, so settled here)

* **Is one completed page the boundary, or its first slice?** The boundary is *two pieces*: the foundation with the smallest real consumer, then one real page. Reason: the first piece must prove the specifier scheme with a real page module and establish the check; the second proves the thing the area note said was impossible (a view converting, with its tests as plain imports) on the page John named.
* **Which page entry first?** `public/workspace-kpis.js` (piece 1), then `public/task-page.js` (piece 2). `app.js` is set aside: it is loaded by 11 renderers, each with its own classic page script after it; making it a module changes when it runs on all 11 at once. `task-page.js` is the last script of one renderer (`lib/render-task-page.js`), reads classic globals only by `typeof window.X` guards, and has no `window.CostFormat` read, so it converts without touching the bridge.
* **Which Waiting entries remain?** Table below: two settled, eight stay with a reason and what would unlock each.

### Direction and the alternatives set aside

**Convert top down (a page entry before the files it uses), serve allow-listed lib leaves at** `/lib/<name>.js`**, import them with relative specifiers (**`../lib/cost-format.js`**), keep** `public/` **flat, test converted views by plain** `import`**.** Each choice, with its reason:

* *Top down, not leaf first.* A leaf converted first has classic consumers; a module runs after every classic script, so each leaf needs a bridge. A page entry converted first runs after `common.js`, so it reads any classic global safely, and the leaves it imports lose their classic consumers one page at a time. Matches John's second survey; I read the same fact in `lib/components/page.js` (`{ module }` is emitted as `<script type="module">`, deferred) and in the consumers (`prompt-section.js` is read by the home, task and swipe pages).
* *Relative specifiers, not an import map.* The map needs an inline script and a CSP hash (`script-src 'self'` plus hashes, `lib/security-headers.js`) and a `package.json` `"imports"` twin for Node. `../lib/x.js` from `/x.js` resolves to `/lib/x.js` in the browser (the URL clamps at the root) and to `lib/x.js` from `public/x.js` in Node, with `"type": "module"` already set. Nothing else to maintain. This costs one rule: `public/` stays flat, so the same string resolves in both places. The rule is checked, not remembered.
* *Re-key* `SHARED_MODULES` *from* `/shared/…` *to* `/lib/…`*, same allow-list, same one-file-per-entry serving.* `/lib` collides with no route (`/library` is a different prefix). `/lib/` is a namespace, never a directory mount: a lib file not on the list stays a 404. The `/shared/` URL is retired in the same change, not kept as an alias.
* *No new bridge entries, one existing entry, deleted when its last classic consumer converts.* A second shared module is never bridged: its twin stays until its last classic consumer is a module. That removes the "one shim per module" question instead of answering it with a general shim. The file keeps its name until it is deleted; renaming a file that is going away touches six renderers for nothing.
* *Native Node import with the existing fake DOM, not a* `vm.SourceTextModule` *loader.* `package.json` is `"type": "module"`, so `import('../../public/x.js')` works once `globalThis.document` is the fake's. A module must not touch `document` at load beyond registering listeners (all the page scripts already work that way). The `vm` loader is flag-gated and exists only to keep script-scope probes (`world.run`) that module scope makes meaningless.
* *Do not relocate the* `common.js` *global pool.* Nothing in these two pieces extracts from `common.js`. A converted page reads classic globals as it does today; extraction happens when a view needs shared logic that has no import path (the timeline maths and `escapeHtml`/format first, per the survey), and only then. Pieces 1–2 therefore add no entry to the bridge.

### The behaviours, and a witness for each (each fails before and passes after)

| \# | Behaviour | Witness |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | The server serves an allow-listed lib leaf at `/lib/<name>.js` with a JavaScript type and the file's exact bytes. | Update `tests/unit/shared-modules.test.js` (express stack and real-server blocks): `/lib/cost-format.js` → 200, bytes equal. Before: 404. |
| 2 | Nothing else under `/lib/` is served, and the retired URL is gone. | Same file, tries what the guard stops: `/lib/vendor-assets.js`, `/lib/render.js`, `/lib/../server.js`, `/lib/%2e%2e/server.js`, `/lib/` and the old `/shared/cost-format.js` are real 404s (not the app shell with 200). |
| 3 | A page module imports a lib leaf by relative specifier and runs under Node. | `public/workspace-kpis.js` becomes a module that imports `formatUsd`; a new test imports it by plain `import()` with the fake DOM, a `Chart` stub and `window.__WORKSPACE_KPI_DATA__`, and reads the tick and tooltip labels. No `window.CostFormat`, no `readyState` setup. Before: the file needs the global and a classic loader. |
| 4 | The same page works in a real browser: MIME, CSP, `/lib/` path, and module order. | The existing `tests/e2e/workspace-kpis.spec.js` cost-axis check (line \~209), rerun against the converted page; it already exists as the witness for module order. If Playwright cannot run in the building session, say so and let CI carry it; do not mark it passed. |

With synthetic failures: a nested `.js`, an import of an un-listed lib file, a bare specifier, an absolute `/shared/…` specifier. |

Witness: 4 (browser) and the page test in 3 (both charts and sparklines drawn).
